message:
test(host): refuse a window three times and it is still allowed

Test 1. The D1 regression in the form the reviewer asked for.

D1 itself landed in c455b78: busy and lingering return Canceled through a separate lambda, and
real failures still return Failed. What was missing is a check of the property rather than of the
mechanism. Two halves existed in different files -- the helper suite asserts a refused capture is
Canceled, the budget suite asserts Canceled costs nothing -- and a reader had to join them.

Now one check does: take the outcome the product actually returned for a refusal, record it three
times the way the control session would, and require the window to still be eligible with no
cooldown. Three is the number that matters. With two dispatchers it takes no time to reach, and if
each refusal cost an attempt the window would go quiet for a minute over a resource conflict it
had no part in -- which is the symptom this whole task exists to prevent, arriving by a different
road.

The outcome is parsed back from the probe rather than typed as a constant, so if the refusal ever
goes back to Failed this fails instead of agreeing with itself.

13 checks, exit 0. Runs a sleeping copy of itself and nothing else: no host, no sockets, no screen
capture, no firewall prompt.
